column2: On the authority of Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, that He said: “O My servants,
I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants,
all of you are astray except those I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants,
all of you are hungry except those I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My servants,
all of you are naked except those I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. O My servants,
you err by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you. O My servants,
you will never attain the power to harm Me so as to harm Me, nor attain the power to benefit Me so as to benefit Me. O My servants,
if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as pious as the most pious heart of any one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in anything. O My servants,
if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man among you, that would not decrease My dominion in anything. O My servants,

if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were to stand together on one plain and ask of Me, and I gave each one what he asked, that would not decrease what I have except as much as a needle decreases [the sea] when it is dipped into the sea. O My servants,

it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay you for in full. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah; and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.” Reported by Muslim.

His words, “from the Prophet ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord”: this hadith is a ḥadīth qudsī, and this phrase is one of the expressions used to introduce a ḥadīth qudsī. Another such expression is

“Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said, in what His Messenger ﷺ relates from Him.” A ḥadīth qudsī is one that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ attributes to his Lord, the Exalted, and ascribes to Him, and that contains first-person pronouns referring to Him, Glorified and Exalted is He.
His words, “O My servants,

I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another”: injustice (ẓulm) is putting a thing in other than its proper place. Allah has forbidden it for Himself and kept Himself from it, though He has power over it and over all things, so injustice never comes from Him at all,

because of the perfection of His justice, Glorified and Exalted is He. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “And Allah wants no injustice for His servants” [Ghāfir 40:31]; and He said: “And your Lord is not unjust to His servants” [Fuṣṣilat 41:46]; and He said: “Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all” [Yūnus 10:44]; and He said:

“Indeed, Allah does not do injustice even the weight of an atom” [al-Nisāʾ 4:40]; and He said: “And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer will fear neither injustice nor deprivation” [Ṭā Hā 20:112], that is, he will fear neither a reduction in his good deeds nor an increase in his bad deeds, nor being made to bear the bad deeds of others.

In denying injustice of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, these verses affirm the perfection of His justice, Glorified is He. Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (2/36): “That He created the actions of His servants, among which is injustice, does not mean that He, Glorified and Exalted is He, is to be described as unjust,
just as He is not described by the other vile acts His servants commit, though they are His creation and His decree; for He is described only by His own actions, not by the actions of His servants.
The actions of His servants are things He has created and made, and He is not described by any of them; He is described only by the attributes and actions that subsist in Him. And Allah knows best.”
Allah the Exalted has forbidden His servants injustice, so no one may wrong himself or wrong anyone else.
His words, “O My servants,
all of you are astray except those I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you”: Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (2/39–40):

“Some have thought that this conflicts with the hadith of ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār from the Prophet ﷺ: ‘Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: I created My servants upright (ḥunafāʾ)—in one narration: Muslims—but the devils led them astray.’

That is not so. Allah created the children of Ādam and gave them a natural disposition (fiṭrah) to accept Islam and incline towards it rather than anything else, with a potential readiness and preparedness for it;
but the servant must still actually be taught Islam, for before being taught he is ignorant and knows nothing, as the Mighty and Majestic said:
‘And Allah brought you out of your mothers' wombs knowing nothing’ [al-Naḥl 16:78]; and He said to His Prophet ﷺ: ‘And He found you unguided and guided [you]’ [al-Ḍuḥā 93:7],

meaning He found you without knowledge of what He then taught you of the Book and wisdom, as the Exalted said: ‘And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith’ [al-Shūrā 42:52].

So a person is born with a natural disposition to accept the truth; if Allah guides him, He provides him with someone to teach him guidance, and he becomes actually guided after having been guided only potentially;

and if Allah forsakes him, He sets over him someone who teaches him what changes his natural disposition, as he ﷺ said: ‘Every child is born upon the fiṭrah, and his parents make him a Jew, a Christian or a Magian.’”

This hadith contains the command to ask Allah for guidance, which includes the guidance of direction and instruction and the guidance of enabling (tawfīq) and keeping on course. The servants' need of guidance is greater than their need of food and drink.

Sūrat al-Fātiḥah contains the words “Guide us to the straight path” [al-Fātiḥah 1:6], in which they ask Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to keep them firm upon the guidance they have and to increase them in guidance upon guidance.
His words, “O My servants,
all of you are hungry except those I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My servants,

all of you are naked except those I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you”: these two sentences show how utterly the servants depend on their Lord and need Him for their provision and clothing, and that they should ask Him, Glorified and Exalted is He, for their food and clothing.
His words, “O My servants,

you err by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you”: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made it obligatory on His servants to carry out the commands and avoid what is prohibited, and the servants fall short in fulfilling what is obligatory on them and fall into some of what they have been forbidden.

The way to safety from that is for them to return to Allah, repent of their sins and ask Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to forgive them. A hadith says: “All the children of Ādam err constantly, and the best of those who err are those who constantly repent.” A ḥasan hadith, recorded by Ibn Mājah (4251) and others.
His words, “O My servants,

you will never attain the power to harm Me so as to harm Me, nor attain the power to benefit Me so as to benefit Me”: Ibn Rajab said (2/43): “That is, the servants are unable to bring Him any benefit or harm,

for Allah the Exalted is in Himself Free of need, Praiseworthy; He has no need of the servants' acts of obedience, and their benefit does not return to Him—it is they who benefit from them; nor is He harmed by their sins—it is they who are harmed by them.

Allah the Exalted said: ‘And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you; indeed, they will never harm Allah at all’ [Āl ʿImrān 3:176]; and He said: ‘And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all’ [Āl ʿImrān 3:144].”
His words, “O My servants,
if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as pious as the most pious heart of any one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in anything. O My servants,

if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man among you, that would not decrease My dominion in anything”: these two sentences make clear the perfection of the dominion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the perfection of His freedom from need of His creation;

that if all the servants were as pious as could be, or as wicked as could be, that would neither increase His dominion in anything nor decrease it; and that each person's piety benefits only that pious person, while the harm of every wicked person's wickedness falls only on himself.
His words, “O My servants,

if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were to stand together on one plain and ask of Me, and I gave each one what he asked, that would not decrease what I have except as much as a needle decreases [the sea] when it is dipped into the sea”: this shows the perfection of the freedom from need of Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, and His servants' need of Him;

and that if the jinn and mankind, from the first of them to the last, gathered together and each asked for what he wanted, and Allah granted it to them, that would not decrease what Allah has except as much as a needle decreases [the sea] when dipped into the sea. The meaning is that no decrease happens at all,
because the water that clings to the mikhyaṭ—the needle—counts for nothing, neither in weight nor to the eye.

His words, “O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay you for in full. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah; and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself”: in this life people are charged with carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions,

and every deed that comes from them, good or bad, is recorded against them, and each will find before him what he sent ahead: if good, then good, and if bad, then bad. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said:

“So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it” [al-Zalzalah 99:7–8]. Whoever sent ahead good will find its reward before him; the reward is from Allah's favour to the servant, and the servant's doing good in this world comes from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, enabling him to do it;

so to Him belongs the favour, first and last. Whoever finds before him something other than good has been brought to it only by his own self, his disobedience to his Lord and the wrong he has done himself; so if he finds punishment before him, let him blame no one but himself.
Among the hadiths are some that the Messenger ﷺ relates from his Lord, containing first-person pronouns referring to Allah; such a hadith is called a ḥadīth qudsī.
Allah has forbidden injustice for Himself and is free of it, and the perfection of its opposite, justice, is affirmed of Him.
Allah has forbidden the servants to wrong themselves or others.
The servants are in great need of asking their Lord for guidance, food, clothing and everything else they need in matters of their religion and worldly life.
Allah loves His servants to ask Him for everything they need in matters of this world and the religion.
The dominion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is perfect; the servants cannot attain the power to benefit or harm Him; rather, their benefit and harm come back on themselves.
The servants are not free from error, and they must repent of it and seek forgiveness.
Piety and wickedness reside in the hearts,
since He said: “as pious as the most pious heart of a man” and “as wicked as the most wicked heart of a man”.
The obedience of the obedient does not increase the dominion of Allah, nor does the disobedience of the disobedient decrease it.

Allah is perfectly free of need and His dominion is perfect: if He gave His servants, from the first to the last, everything they asked of Him, it would not decrease the dominion and treasuries of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in anything.
The servants are urged to obey and warned against disobedience, and all of it is recorded against them.

Whoever Allah enables to follow the path of good wins the happiness of this world and the Hereafter; the favour belongs to Allah for enabling him to follow the path of guidance and for granting the reward for it.
Whoever falls short and does evil gains only loss, and regrets when regret is of no use.
